title: Timeline write admission regresses after cache policy repair
fault_primitive: A detached process in social-graph-mongodb periodically publishes Redis min-replicas-to-write=1 to both standalone timeline caches
incident_class: Leftover operational policy synchronization applies a replicated-store durability contract to standalone ephemeral caches
symptoms: All pods remain Running and Ready. Redis remains master and can answer reads and health checks, but rejects timeline writes and cache population with NOREPLICAS. Posting and some cold timeline reads fail, producing frontend and user-timeline errors. Repairs to runtime policy or restarts of destination caches work temporarily and regress within six minutes.
why_hard: No Deployment, ConfigMap, Service, collection, or role change identifies the source. The failing dependency names the immediate write-admission problem but not the remote policy writer. A repair can pass a complete two-minute SLO window before the dormant six-minute publisher restores the setting. The publisher lives in an existing relationship database container and follows stable Service DNS across cache replacement.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Restore Redis write admission and submit after immediate request checks
Restart or roll back timeline caches and services
Add replicas to satisfy an unintended quorum policy
Inspect Kubernetes controllers and static configuration without checking unmanaged processes
mitigation_summary: Find and terminate the detached cache-policy-sync process inside social-graph-mongodb, remove its temporary operational files, and set min-replicas-to-write back to the stock standalone-cache default of zero on both timeline Redis instances. No saved state, data deletion, or original manifests are needed.
